issues.legal_issue: A statutory notice is not required before a suit challenging a municipal body's interference with claimed private ownership or possession when the challenged conduct is not alleged to have been done under the municipal statute.
material_facts: The suit sought a permanent injunction against obstruction of the plaintiff's claimed possession and enjoyment of property.
The dispute concerned who owned and possessed the property, and the plaintiff did not allege that the municipal body acted under the municipal statute.
The municipal body relied on the statutory notice requirement, while the High Court considered an analogy with the notice requirement for suits against the government.
issues.conclusion: No notice under Section 447 of the Hyderabad Municipal Corporation Act was necessary before the suit was instituted.
issues.legal_principle: Section 447 requires notice for suits concerning acts done or purportedly done in execution or intended execution of the Act, or an alleged neglect or default in its execution. A dispute over private ownership and possession, where the challenged conduct is not alleged to have been under the Act, does not fall within that requirement. The statutory powers concerning parks or removal of obstructions did not establish that the conduct in dispute was under the Act. No earlier case was relied on.

predicates.suit_for_injunction_against_municipal_bo: A plaintiff brought a suit seeking an injunction against a municipal body.
predicates.dispute_concerns_private_title_or_posses: The parties' dispute concerned who owned or possessed the property.
predicates.challenged_conduct_not_under_statutory_f: The plaintiff did not allege that the municipal body's challenged conduct was done under its statutory functions.
predicates.prior_notice_not_required: A notice need not be given before the suit is instituted.

issues.definition: When an injunction suit against a municipal body concerns private title or possession and the challenged conduct is not alleged to be under its statutory functions, prior notice is not required.

issues.legal_issue: An executive order concerning property is not a legislative enactment, and its legal effect and evidentiary value must be determined by the courts as an executive act.
material_facts: An order approved proposals to transfer a prohibited area along a river to the municipal body for public use.
The High Court treated the order as expressing the ruler's will and therefore as law.
The municipal body accepted before the Supreme Court that the order was an executive act, not legislation.
issues.conclusion: The order could not be treated as a legislative enactment; its effect as an executive order and its evidentiary value had to be determined by the courts.
issues.legal_principle: The order's legal effect had to be assessed in its character as an executive act, including its evidentiary value on the dispute. The judgment cites no provision or earlier case for this holding.

predicates.executive_order_at_issue: A party relied on an executive order affecting property relevant to the dispute.
predicates.legal_effect_of_order_disputed: The parties disputed the legal effect of that executive order.
predicates.executive_order_is_not_legislation_and_i: The order is not treated as legislation, and its effect is determined by the courts as an executive act.

issues.definition: When an executive order affecting property is at issue and its legal effect is disputed, the order is not treated as legislation and its effect is assessed by the courts.

issues.legal_issue: A property dispute must be remanded for fresh determination when inadequate investigation and an incomplete record leave material questions of title and possession unresolved.
material_facts: The appeal arose from a suit concerning title to and possession of disputed property.

The record included old documents, but the sale deed's referenced plan and mortgage were not produced, relevant agreements were missing, and the relationship between the claimed property and land for which compensation had been paid was unresolved.
The courts below had not adequately investigated or assessed the central factual disputes, including the extent and location of the property.
The Supreme Court considered that a local investigation by a commissioner could assist if a party applied for one.
issues.conclusion: The appeal was allowed and the case was remanded to the trial court to decide title and possession afresh, with further evidence and any requested commissioner investigation confined to those issues.
issues.legal_principle: Where the record and the courts' inquiry do not adequately resolve the real factual controversy, the matter may be remanded for fresh determination. The remand was confined to title and possession; the parties could provide relevant evidence and seek a commissioner, and could seek only amendments strictly necessary to clarify those issues without changing the nature of the case. No provision or earlier case was relied on for this direction.

predicates.appeal_from_property_title_and_possessio: An appeal arose from a suit in which title to and possession of property were disputed.
predicates.material_title_or_possession_questions_u: Material questions about the parties' title or possession remained unresolved.
predicates.record_or_inquiry_inadequate: The evidence or investigation below was insufficient to resolve those material questions.
predicates.case_remanded_for_fresh_determination_of: The case is sent back for a fresh decision on title and possession.

issues.definition: When an appeal from a property title and possession suit presents unresolved material questions on an inadequate record or inquiry, the case is remanded for a fresh decision on title and possession.
